pages.title: CPS
pages.text: The $(item)Radio Programmer$() floppy installs $(thing)CPS$(), the programming software radio shops use. It reads and writes the channels of a $(l:radiocraft:radios/commercial_radios)commercial radio$(): 16, or 64 on the upgraded handheld (the list scrolls; A to D mark where each zone starts).$(br2)$(thing)F5$() reads a radio and $(thing)F6$() writes it. A placed mobile is reached by its programming cable: touching the computer, or on its $(l:radiocraft:radios/data_wire)data wire$().

pages.title: Radios in your hand
pages.text: A handheld, or a mobile still in item form, is read or written by hand. With no radio wired (or $(thing)A radio in your hand$() picked), F5 or F6 asks you to press $(thing)Continue$(): the screen closes, then right click the computer or its monitor holding the radio. CPS opens again with its channels read, or says it was written. It waits 60 seconds.$(br2)For a fleet, $(thing)F9$() turns on $(thing)Program radios$(): Close, then each click writes a radio (sneak to read one), until CPS closes or after five minutes unused.

Enter edits a channel: its name (8 letters), receive and transmit frequencies (transmit blank for simplex, RX for receive only), FM or DIG, a CTCSS tone, and on digital channels an encryption key with whether it may be read back. Del clears one, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy one. A write is all or nothing, and the radio refuses what it cannot do (a frequency out of its bands, digital on the basic brick).

pages.title: Unit IDs
pages.text: Every commercial radio sends its $(thing)unit ID$() (1-9999) each time it keys up: a short data burst on FM, inside the data on digital. Radios with a display show who is talking, by ID or by the name in their $(thing)contact list$(). $(thing)F4$() sets the ID CPS writes; programming radios by hand, it goes up by one after each radio. Left at 0, each radio keeps its own (a new radio gets one). $(thing)F7$() edits the contact list.

pages.title: Hidden keys
pages.text: A key set as not readable shows as $(thing)****$(): it never comes off the radio. Write the channels back and the radio keeps its own key; type a new key over it to change it. A hidden key cannot be copied to another radio.$(br2)Ctrl+S saves the channels as a $(thing)codeplug$() (.CPG) to load into other radios of the fleet; a 64-channel codeplug loaded for a 16-channel radio leaves out what does not fit. F8 erases a wired radio back to factory blank.
A blank floppy and a comparator.
